intended_object: The canonical R-algebra isomorphism between the level-three ring R[u][μ]/(μ³(μ³+8)³ − u(μ³−1)³) and the localization R[μ][(μ³−1)⁻¹], valid when 3 is invertible in R. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The forward map is `lift` applied to the image of X. It sends μ to X/1, which is allowed because X³−1 is a unit in the localization. It also sends u to X³(X³+8)³/(X³−1)³. The backward map is the universal map out of the localization. It sends X to μ, which is allowed because μ³−1 is a unit in the level-three ring when 3 is invertible.

The proof checks that both composites are the identity. One direction uses the extension principle for maps out of a localization. The other uses `algHom_ext`, which needs only agreement on μ together with x³−1 being a unit.

So this is exactly the canonical isomorphism described in the docstring, with μ ↦ X. The hypothesis that 3 is a unit is genuinely needed. Without it the statement fails: modulo 3 the quotient has points with μ = 1 and arbitrary u, as the module documentation notes. R is an arbitrary commutative ring, so the generality is natural. Mathlib has no counterpart for this specific ring.
